bib.title: PYMT5: multi-mode translation of natural language and PYTHON code with transformers

question: Can one text-to-text transformer, pre-trained with span masking on Python and trained to translate between all method features, both generate method bodies from docstrings and summarize code into docstrings better than GPT2 baselines?
hypothesis: Treating Python and docstrings as natural languages in one shared vocabulary, with multi-mode training and pre-training, beats single-task autoregressive baselines.
contributions: PYMT5, a multi-mode Python method text-to-text transformer
Largest parallel corpus of Python methods and docstrings (26M methods, 7.7M with docstrings)
Control-token prefixes for style-conditioned docstring generation
25x faster docstring-generation convergence from span-masking pre-training

method.summary: A 374M encoder-decoder transformer is pre-trained with T5-style span masking on 27GB of Python files, then trained on method-docstring pairs to translate between all feature pairs of signature, docstring and body, steered by a '# target <feature> (<style>)' comment prefix. Compared with GPT2-medium (random or English initialised) on method and docstring generation.
method.task: method generation from signature+docstring; docstring generation from signature+body

datasets.name: GitHub Python corpus
datasets.size: 2.3 million unique files, about 27GB raw text (from 5.3M files, 112k of 118k repos cloned)
datasets.split: 90% train / 5% val / 5% test, split by repository
datasets.source: public GitHub repos labelled primarily Python, at least 10 stars, commit in past 5 years
datasets.preprocessing: literal duplicate files removed, finer clones kept; license text removed

datasets.name: PyMT5 method-docstring corpus
datasets.split: 90/5/5 by repository; test set 1,285,794 methods (method gen), 383695 methods (docstring gen)
datasets.source: ast extraction from the same files
datasets.preprocessing: ast + astunparse so no syntactically incorrect code is seen; 2to3 and autopep8 for failed parses (97.3% parsed); comments ignored; docstrings cleaned of non-ASCII, unicode normalised, commit hashes/paths/URLs replaced by placeholders

datasets.name: CodeSearchNet Python test
datasets.size: 500k Python methods with docstrings in CSN
datasets.preprocessing: CSN removed methods with 'test' in the name and under 3 lines

datasets.name: Barone and Sennrich test
datasets.size: about 200x smaller than the authors' test set

models.name: PyMT5
models.init_from: span-masking pre-trained on 27GB Python; all experiments start from it
models.tokenizer: BPE trained on raw Python files (extended GPT tokenizer with whitespace tokens)

models.name: GPT2-medium random init
models.tokenizer: extended GPT2 tokenizer with whitespace tokens

training.objective: Pre-training: T5-style span masking, random spans up to length 3 replaced by numbered mask tokens, target is mask followed by replaced tokens. Fine-tuning: multi-mode translation between all signature/docstring/body combinations with no shared feature (Table 5), '# target <feature> (<style>)' prefix.
training.steps: docstring-only run converged at 3.97e5 steps from random init; pre-trained reached the best validation loss at 1.5e4 steps
training.epochs: pre-training 73 epochs; multi-mode PyMT5 62 epochs; docstring-only 183 epochs random vs 7 epochs pre-trained
training.hardware: pre-training: sixteen 32GB Tesla V100; multi-mode PyMT5: 16 Tesla V100 16GB; GPT2: 4 Tesla V100 16GB each
training.wall_clock: pre-training 3 weeks; multi-mode 5 weeks; GPT2 baselines 1 week (7 days)

other.hyperparameters: fairseq-train scripts are in Figs 7 and 8 as images; not in the text layer
other.note: pre-training hardware printed as 32GB V100 in Sec 2.2 and multi-mode as 16GB V100 in Sec 3/A.4

inference.decoding: beam search, beam width 5 (stated for the method-generation section)
inference.prompting: comment prefix '# target <feature> (<style>)'; style imperative only when docstring is in the target

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: n-gram overlap of generated vs reference

metrics.name: Syntax
metrics.definition: fraction of predicted methods with correct syntax under Python 3.7 grammar

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: model perplexity on own test set

eval.protocol: Single runs; the authors say GPT2 variants differ within margin of error; no seeds or significance test stated.

results.claim: On the CodeSearchNet test set the best model reaches BLEU 8.59 for method generation.
results.setup: CSN Python test, method from signature+docstring, PyMT5 374M, beam 5
results.quote: achieved a BLEU score of 8.59 for method generation

results.claim: On the CSN test set PyMT5 gets BLEU 16.3 for docstring generation.
results.setup: CSN Python test, docstring from signature+body

results.claim: 92.1% of PyMT5 method bodies on CSN are syntactically correct.
On the authors' own test set (1,285,794 methods) PyMT5 more than doubles GPT2 BLEU and is 93.6% syntactically correct vs 86%.
results.note: Syntax for GPT2 given as 86% in text; 85%/86% in table for random/English

results.claim: Pre-trained initialisation reached the best validation loss 25x faster for docstring generation.
results.setup: single seq2seq of PyMT5 architecture on docstrings only, random vs pre-trained init

results.claim: English pre-trained GPT2 barely beats random init on Python.
results.table: Table 3, row GPT2-med english, column BLEU
results.note: authors say metrics are almost all within margin of error

results.claim: Restricting own test set to CSN-style curation drops ROUGE F-scores toward CSN values, suggesting tests and short methods are easier.

limits: Only GPT2-medium baselines trained on same data; no comparison to other code models; single runs, no significance test.
Perplexity, BLEU and ROUGE only; no execution-based evaluation, only syntax validity.
Barone test set may leak into the training set (authors' hypothesis) and is small.
TransS3 ROUGE-L 51.27 not comparable because it does not state which statistic.
Fairseq hyperparameters are only in images (Figs 7, 8); optimizer, lr, batch size not in text.
Finer-grained code clones were not removed.

terms.definition: training to translate between all pairs of feature combinations of signature, docstring and body where the same feature is not in both source and target

figures.caption: Denoising auto-encoder pre-training for sequence-to-sequence tasks, based on the span-masking objective used by the T5
figures.why: shows span masking on tokenized Python

figures.caption: Real examples of PYMT5 performing method generation using combinations of signatures and docstrings
Learning curves for training a sequence-to-sequence transformer, translating from python method definitions to their docstrings

problems: fairseq training scripts (Figs 7, 8) are images, so optimizer, lr and batch size are not in the text.
Text says 1/10th of corpus is 700k docstrings but Fig 4 caption says 770k.
Pre-training GPU memory 32GB vs multi-mode 16GB; Table 1 caption says 3x as large as next largest while text says twice.
